label: text
text:
On Wednesday two further
cuses of enteric fever (typhoid).
were notified. Both patients were
Chinese, from the city district.

label: text
text: The “Times of Malaya” understands that the Government is reducing the charge for electric light in Iph to 20 cents per unit as from August 1.

label: text
text: The "Times" contains an advertisement for assistant engineers for P.W.D. of the F.M.S. for four years' service on a beginning salary of $400 a month.

label: text
text: Thirty bags of letters dated London, July 29, were included in a total of 133 bags brought by the s.s. "Tilawn" yesterday. The Home paper mail of the same date is due on Sunday.

label: text
text: Shop fittings, furniture, tables, bedstands, carpets, etc., will be sold by auction at Messrs. Lane, Crawford Ltd.—old premises — by Messrs. Lammert Bros., at noon tomorrow.

label: text
text: Nairobi, August 12. — The lengthy trial of a native, charged with outraging an elderly European lady, aged 70 years, twice in a single night, and also with brutally assaulting her, concluded to day when the accused was found guilty and sentenced to 14 years' imprisonment and 24 lashes. This case, which occurred in Kijube on May 17, was one of the chief causes of anxiety regarding the safety of white women, which resulted in Government action and the revision of the law recently "any unced.

label: text
text: London, August 12. — Mr. Havelock Wilson, addressing seamen at Middlesbrough, said that one of the greatest misfortunes of the Labour movements was its entry into politics. The Trades Unions were now in a very serious condition, nearly everyone of them being bankrupt; worse still, hundreds of thousands of men had declared that they would never pay anything more into the Unions. Labour and Capital were mutually indispensable. "Let us try and foster a better understanding with the employers," added Mr. Wilson. "This is the one way in which the Unions can recover. I am glad to say that we have arrived at something like an intelligent position in the shipping industry."

label: text
text: Further evidence was taken at the Kowloon Magistracy yesterday afternoon in the case in which four men are charged with committing an armed robbery at the residence of in Chinese merchant, his wife and daughter, from whom they are alleged to have stolen valuables and money to a total of $1,500. The case will be continued this afternoon, when it is expected it will be concluded.

label: text
text: Lieut. Comdr. C. E. Allen has been appointed to H.M.S. "Titania" for command of a submarine.

label: text
text: Mr. Geo. W. Grey, F. S. I., Architect to the Hongkong Realty and Trust Company, Ltd., has been elected a Member of The Royal Sanitary Institute. We understand his election was owing to his work, and writings, in connection with sanitation and plumbing, relating to public health.

label: text
text: In the Cooperative Hall, Methil, Fifeshire, five miners who were sent to prison under the Emergency Regulations during the general strike for holding up traffic and throwing stones at the police, were acclaimed as heroes and presented with medals provided through the International Class-War Prisoner's Aid. There was a large gathering, and the speeches were interspersed with the singing of the Red Flag.

label: text
text:
Commissions as Second-Lieutenants in the S.S. Volunteer Force Reserve of Officers, have been granted to the following: Mr. C. A. Scott, Mr. James Pearce, Mr. A. W. Frisby, Mr. C. A. Reuters and Mr. A. A. de Cruez, all of Penang.
Carlias, Venezuela, August 15. - The German ex-Chancellor, Dr. Luther, who is visiting the chief German settlements in South America, has been the principal guest at "many functions." Dr. Luther visited President Gomez and is now on his way to Colombia.

label: text
text: The many friends of Mrs. Burton, wife of Mr. L. A. Burton, of the Hongkong Treasury, will be interested to hear that she has succeeded in passing the London College of Music examination for piano-playing. She has been made an Associate and has received the College diploma.

label: text
text: A distingħed officer of the Indian Medical Service recently undertook an enquiry into "Heat-stroke in Allahabad Independent Brigade Area in relation to meteorological conditions." The following is an extract from his report which has just been published:—"Unfortunately meteorological conditions in 1925 were unfavourable for the occurrence of heat-stroke and only one "case occurred in Benares during June."

label: text
text: Miss Mitchell, who already holds the French speed record for typing, beat her own record at the recent congress of the Stenoeraphic Federation held at Auxerre, when she made 882 taps to the minute, or 14.7 per second.

label: text
text: It is proposed to hold two competitions in design each year among the drawing office staff of the Singapore Municipal Architect, at an annual cost of about $250.

label: text
text: Hankow, August 14.—Reports received by the local Chinese newspaper states that Mr. Chiang Tsopin, leader, the Kuomintang, has been appointed as pacification commissioner of Hupeh by the Canton Nationalist Government.

label: text
text: Dairen, August 16.—Through the Japanese Consul-General at Mukden, the Kwangtung Government tendered a formal protest to-day to the Mukden authorities against "the drastic measures taken by them to check the steady decline of the Mukden notes. The protest, pointing out the arrest of the clerks of the Japanese exchange brokers and the temporary closing of the Japanese exchanges, demanded that the authorities take more moderate steps in future.

label: text
text: Sentence of six months rigorous imprisonment was on August 19 passed on E. D. Sykes who was convicted by the Singapore District Judge, Mr. P. F. David on three charges of cheating by tendering cheques in payment of debts when he had no funds in the bank to meet the cheques. Sykes had a sum of $1,700 in the bank, it was said, and during history in Singapore, doing business as an import and export broker, he had distributed cheques amounting to over $18,000.

label: paragraph_title
text: SOCIAL AND PERSONAL NEWS.

label: text
text: Peking, August 16.—Mr. F. Hussey-Freke, formerly secretary of the Hailo Conservancy Commission, Tientsin, signed a contract yesterday evening appointing him Associate Chief Inspector of the Salt Gabelle. He assumed office this morning.

label: text
text: The Hongkong Radio Society is transmitting a programme of gramophone records between 7 and 8 this evening.

label: text
text: Nauen, August 4.—A Carnegie professorial chair will be inaugurated at Berlin's University of Politics, “Dentsche Honnschule fuer Politik” following the recent visit of President of the Carnegie Fund, Nicholas Murray Butler. Each year an internationally known authority on ethnology will lecture at Berlin, as was done before the war.

label: text
text: London, August 13. — Mr. Quaritch on behalf of an English customer has again acquired the "Pilgrim's Progress" copy for a smaller amount than auctioned on July 26. The price is not disclosed.—"Times of Ceylon."

label: text
text: A reference to a mounted white tiger being on "show in India," called forth a letter to the "Statesman," Calcutta, from a correspondent who says that recently two such white tigers have been shot in the Pasan Zemindary, Central Provinces, Bilaspore District. The skin is practically white chocolate (not black) stripes very prettily marked, a most handsome specimen, all else is normal including the eyes. Information frequently comes in of other tigers of the same colour having been seen, in the same forests. The correspondent raises the question of whether this is a distinct species.

label: text
text: London, August 12.—There has been an unusual sequel to the sale of “Pilgrim's Progress,” mentioned in the message of July 26, the buyer having returned it to the auctioneers on the ground that it was not a first edition, but a second issue of the first edition. The existence of this issue, which is distinguished by a five-line errata at the end, was hitherto not generally known to bibliographers. The book is still worth a thousand sterling, but is scarcely as valuable as the original first edition.

label: text
text: Geneva, August 6.—Tass, the official Russian news agency will not be represented at the League of Nations Commission of News Agencies to convene at Geneva on August 19 for the purpose of securing improvements in international press facilities.

label: text
text: London, August 10.—Rome.—Commenting on the Italian and Spanish Treaty, the “Glornal d’Italia” remarks that many countries have Mediterranean interests, notably, Great Britain, whose watchfulness towards communications to India nobody can dispute, but defines the principal aim of the present Treaty to be the shifting of the equilibrium in the Mediterranean by a joint effort of two sister nations.

label: text
text: Cairo. — Considerable feeling has been created in Egyptian circles by personal attacks on ping Fuad in connection with the exchange of a Crown building (for the purposes of the Egyptian University) for State lands alleged to be worth six times the value of the building. The question was raised in the Chamber and this has been followed by a violent Press war around the person of the King.

label: text
text: By 187 votes to 173, the Wesleyan Methodist Conference at York recently adopted a recommendation that women should be made eligible for the ministry of the Wesleyan Church as far as possible on the same terms as men. The recommendation contained the qualification that the marriage of a woman minister should be regarded as equivalent to resignation or withdrawal from active ministry.

label: text
text: Excavators working on the Roman amphitheatre at Caerleon—the site of which was purchased for the nation by "The Daily Mail"—found an inscribed stone on the original road surface in the middle of the recently opened entrance to the arena. The stone is inscribed with a man's name, reading "U. Hentulium." In the opinion of those in charge of the excavation, the stone was probably carved not as part of an official work but just as a signature. Another interesting find was a Bin-long bronze pin, with a decorated end.

label: text
text: Mr. H. F. Monk has been appointed a Police magistrate for Penang.

label: text
text: It is not true that the Singapore Police Band has been engaged to play in Hongkong.

label: text
text: Dr. W. M. Lupton, temporary Medical Officer, has been second-ed for service under the Government of Kedah.—P. G.

label: text
text: A promenade concert at Volunteer Headquarters on September 24 is announced in current corps orders. It will be held by the Infantry Co. Tickets are at 50 cents each.

label: text
text: Bombay, August 13.—The new Governor-General of Portuguese India, Senor Massano De Amori, arrived to-day and received officers of the Consulate and representatives of the Bombay Government.

label: text
text: Dr. Fitzpatrick is now in charge of the District Hospital, Kuala Lumpur. Dr. Fitzpatrick is the sixth medical officer to hold this appointment in the last eight months. The hospital has nearly 1,000 beds.—M.M.

label: text
text: Major-General Sir Charles Herbert Powell, K.C.B., a veteran of the British Army, who was Staff-Officer in China, 1900-1, was injured by a taxicab almost immediately upon his arrival at San Francisco. Travelling with the general from Shanghai, were Mr. and Mrs. E. F. Bothwell, en route to England.

label: text
text: The Singapore Band shows definite promise of coming into being. A short time ago about twenty more bandsmen arrived from India and there is now a strength of twenty-six players. Four players are still required to play the bassoon, bass, French horn and cornet. A good deal of spade work has yet to be done before any public performances can be attempted. It is hoped, however, that by the beginning of next year the band will come into full service. We are assured that when it does make an appearance, it will be well worth hearing.
